The reason why I always go with $5 mil has to do with inflation. Even assuming that we average 3.5% inflation, and assuming that people keep their money fully invested in the stock market through retirement age, and assuming the stock market averages 9% return, and assuming you refuse to touch the principle, this gives you a 1.5% payout in dividends each year. 5 mil * 1.5% = $75,000/ year. Of course, there are a lot of assumptions here, and changing them can easily change the outcome. If you are older, then you could heavily weight your portfolio toward dividend paying stocks, and bring the 1.5% up to 5%, and assuming you only need $48k per year, then you would only need about $1 million to retire.
